h1: What could a website bring in?
lead: Most customers look a business up before they call. Put in your own numbers to see what a good website could be worth to you, and when it pays for itself.
title: Website Calculator: What Could a Website Bring In? | Ambs Solutions
description: Work out what a website could bring in for your trade or small business. Move the sliders to match your visitors, enquiries and job value, and see when it pays for itself.

blocks.heading: Try it with your own numbers
blocks.text: The sliders start as an example for a cabinet maker. Move them to match a normal month for your business.
blocks.note: Example figures to show how the sum works, not a promise. Results depend on your trade, your area and the website.

blocks.heading: Three ways a website moves these numbers

items.title: More visitors
items.text: A page for each service and area you cover, and a Google Business Profile that links to your site, so locals find you when they search.

items.title: More enquiries
items.text: Tap to call and a short quote form on every page, sized for phones, so people get in touch while they are keen.

items.title: More jobs won
items.text: Real photos of your work, Google reviews and clear details, so people trust you before the first call.

items.a: No. The sliders start with example numbers to show how the sum works. In a free session we look at your business and work out an estimate together.

items.q: Where do I find my website visitor numbers?
items.a: Google Analytics or Google Search Console shows how many people visit your site each month. If you do not have a website yet, start the visitors slider low.

items.q: What does the website cost slider mean?
items.a: Put in the price you have been quoted for a website. The chart shows the month when the work it brings in adds up to more than that price.

items.q: Does this work for my trade?
items.a: Yes. The sum is the same for any business that takes enquiries: builders, electricians, plumbers, cabinet makers, cafés, clinics and more. Change the job value to suit your work.
